body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.headline: County Board Votes to Add Philosophy to Middle-School Curriculum
paras: The Maplewood County Board of Education **voted 5–2** on Wednesday to **introduce** a year-long philosophy course for **eighth graders** from next autumn. **Proponents** say the course will **sharpen reasoning**; **opponents**, who **cited** budget pressures, **warned** it would **crowd out** the arts.

Superintendent Carla Dunn **told the board** that a pilot in two schools had **yielded** “markedly better” classroom discussion, **though** she **conceded** the sample was small. **Teachers will receive** a stipend for training. **The measure takes effect** in September, **subject to** final budget approval. (Fictional report.)

items.q: The course is for eighth graders.
The superintendent admits that the pilot sample was small.

head: Recurso
Exemplo
Função
rows: **though** she conceded the sample was small

blocks.body: Notícias combinam **fatos verificáveis** (números, datas) e **vozes atribuídas**. *Though* introduz um contraponto sem abandonar a fonte. A leitura mantém **ritmo regular** e **queda de tom** ao fim de cada informação.
*Introduce* = “implantar, apresentar”; “introduzir” em outros contextos pode ser *insert*. Cuidado: *Introduce* alguém = apresentar.

items.s: The board ___ 5–2 to add the course. (vote)
She ___ that the sample was small. (concede)
The measure is ___ to final budget approval. (subject)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Carry the vote.** — Vencer a votação.
**Sit on the fence.** — Ficar em cima do muro.
**Put to a vote.** — Pôr em votação.
**Table a motion.** — Adiar uma moção.
**Pass with flying colours.** — Passar com louvor.
**Win by a narrow margin.** — Vencer por pouco.
**Go to the polls.** — Ir às urnas.
**Take effect.** — Entrar em vigor.
**On the cards.** — Provável.
**Face opposition.** — Enfrentar oposição.
**How did the vote go?** — Como foi a votação?
**Five to two in favour.** — Cinco a dois a favor.
**What did the opponents say?** — O que os opositores disseram?

items.note: Ajuste refinado de entonação: pequenas variações de altura e de ritmo mudam a atitude (cortesia, ironia, reserva, compromisso) sem mudar as palavras.
words: I suppose that’s one way to put it. ↘↗ (reserva)
Well, that’s ONE way to put it. ↘ (ironia)

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence news report on a fictional local decision, with a vote count, two views and a condition.
blocks.model: The city council voted 6–3 on Tuesday to ban cars from the old square. Proponents say the move will cut noise. Opponents, who cited lost trade, warned of empty shops. The mayor conceded that the data were limited. The ban takes effect in May, subject to a safety review. A public hearing is planned.

items.q: What does “county board of education” mean?
items.why: **county board of education** = conselho de educação do condado.
**middle-school curriculum** = currículo do ensino fundamental II.
